title: OSIRIS v4.3.0: a governed local console for a living language model
description:
OSIRIS is a local-first console built around a small language model (osiris.nclm) that learns from every conversation and from the author's documents, and answers in its own voice only after passing a held-out test (30 held-out exchanges at ≤ 2.0 bits/byte and below a unigram baseline). Until then a local Ollama model speaks for it, labelled as such, and the core trains on its replies. Deterministic code chooses and runs read-only checks (training status, git history, ledger integrity, system load, named files), retrieves grounding notes with file citations, and appends every exchange to a SHA-256 hash chain.

New in v4.3.0: a claims register and physics checks. OSIRIS holds 32 claims from the author's own work, each with a verdict (supported, reported, null, refuted, artifact, not measured, ruled out by a computed bound, overclaim, no evidence, untested, pilot), the finding, and the evidence: Zenodo DOIs, and files whose SHA-256 is computed when the entry is shown. Deterministic checks compute the bounds a claim must respect: radiated thrust at most P/c, rim speed against c, the mass-energy implied by a static metric perturbation, the CHSH local and Tsirelson bounds, efficiency at most 100 %, the log2(shots) ceiling on measured entropy, and whether a dynamical-decoupling sequence fits its idle window. A message that mentions a registered claim gets its verdict from code before any model answers, and the model is held to it (/legit, /physics). Also new: an evidence probe for pre-registered results, paired pre/post scoring of the core (used by NCLM-GATE-PILOT-0, 10.5281/zenodo.23075229), and the NCLM-Mix-1 pre-registration (not yet run).

Measured state at release: the core has not passed its gate. In NCLM-GATE-PILOT-0, training on the exchanges improved the core on held-out replies by 0.043 bits/byte, but at 5.3-5.6 bits/byte it was still worse than a unigram model of the same replies (4.45-4.58). The pre-registered learning test (NCLM-1) has not been run. Earlier CRSM-era constants and metrics kept in the repository (tau-phase anomaly, theta_lock = 51.843 deg, CCCE metrics) were refuted on hardware by the author and are not claimed.
